verified.title: The generator join to the reference fires is an unchecked inner join: a fired test event with no prediction row silently lowers n, down to n=0 with empty done.json metrics and exit 0
verified.detail: cgen.py:93-96 and cparam.py:93-97 join the test prediction rows to the referenced classifier's fired rows with `how="inner"` and take `n = joined.height`, with nothing comparing that count against the referenced report's `frozen[risk]["n"]`. Every fired test event whose example_id is absent from this eval's own prediction frame is dropped without a word. Two reachable routes, both passing all three of probe_eval's gates (done.json present, risk_targets equal, build key equal), because both train runs come from the same build: (a) `train.predict.splits` (experimental_settings/schema.py:96, default `["val","test"]`) is a settable list -- a generator run written with `predict.splits: [val]` (the cost of generating at every cut row is 9(a)#2's named fallback) produces a report whose `exact` block is all null with `n: 0` at every risk, `done.json` `metrics: {}`, and a zero exit; (b) errata entry 118 puts the `train.max_len` overlong drop inside each method's own batching, over that method's own text, so a cgen run and the ctool run it references drop different events even at identical settings, and those events "get no prediction row". Contract 1.4's whole point for the shared-build-key gate is that "the join partly succeeds ... a wrong exact-match number with no error anywhere", and ticket 10's M-E2 states the acceptance as `exact` numbers "with the same n as the classifier's frozen n at that risk" -- nothing in the shipped code enforces that. Note the ticket pins the inner join (section 1 step 4), so this is a missing check rather than a deviation from the ticket; the fix is a comparison of the joined height against `ref_fields["frozen"][risk_str]["n"]`, or a refusal naming the fired example_ids that have no prediction row.

verdict.reason:
Mechanism reproduced, rule claim refuted — this is a design proposal, not a defect against any pinned rule.

WHAT I REPRODUCED (synthetic frames, cgen.report called directly, open_env stubbed, nothing written anywhere): with a val-only prediction frame the block is `{'tool_ok': None, 'params_all_ok': None, 'full_call_ok': None, 'n': 0, 'ci': None}`, `_generator_metrics` returns `{}`; with one fired example_id absent from the prediction frame, `exact` carries `n: 1` against the reference's `frozen` `n: 2`. So yes, the inner join lowers n and nothing compares it to `frozen[risk]["n"]` (eval/methods/cgen.py:93-96, eval/methods/cparam.py:96-98).

WHY IT IS NOT A FINDING:

1. The ticket pins exactly this code. .scratch/from-zero/issues/10-eval-generators-scorer-and-table.md step 4: "Otherwise join `test` to `ref_fires.filter(risk == risk, split == \"test\")` on `example_id` ... and report the three rates rounded to 4 with `n` = joined rows". No comparison is asked for. The finding concedes this ("the ticket pins the inner join ... a missing check rather than a deviation").

2. Contract 1.4 says the same and no more: "`eval/methods/cgen.py` and `eval/methods/cparam.py` join their own prediction rows to this table on `example_id` and report exact match over the joined rows" (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:1378-1380). 1.4 also blesses an `n: 0` block with three null fields, null `ci` and no refusal as a legitimate uniform shape for the null-theta case (:1327-1334), so an n=0 generator block is not an error signal in this format.

3. M-E2 is not a code requirement. In ticket 10 it sits under the header "### GPU / main session — not yours" (issues/10-...md:634-638), and the wave-4 reconciliation comment says "`M-E2` and `M-E3` stay with the GPU list after wave 6" (:692-693). It is a human acceptance read on a real matched run — a person comparing the two reports — not a check the implementer was told to write. It is also on the already-known list (the precheck's T10-7: M-E2 cannot show a --debug eval row through table(), owner's call).

4. Errata entry 118 makes a differing drop set the designed outcome, not an unchecked bug: "`train.max_len` ... applied in each method's `batches` over the longest text of the event; those rows get no prediction row and the count is `done.json`'s `counts.dropped_overlong`". A strict `n == frozen["n"]` refusal would contradict that ruling, since an honest cgen run at identical settings is expected to keep a different row set from the ctool run it references.

5. Route (a) is an operator setting, and the contract already ruled how empty val/test is prevented — upstream, at the split defaults, not with an eval-side guard: contracts :1899-1910 and 9(a)#44/#47 (:5047-5059) walk through "a single-split `sample` run ... `train.predict.splits` writes no prediction rows, and the eval fits a temperature on nothing" and fix it by keeping three splits in the debug walk.

6. "Silently ... no message anywhere" is inaccurate. probe_eval._render_report_md prints the per-risk line with `n=0` and an "## events per split" block listing only `val` — my reproduction printed "- risk 0.05: ... n=0" and "- val: 2". The n that M-E2's human comparison needs is in the report.

The contract 1.4 quote the finding leans on ("the join partly succeeds ... a wrong exact-match number with no error anywhere", contracts :2155-2159) belongs to the shared-build-key gate and names a different failure: ids that mean different cuts. That gate is implemented (eval/utils/probe_eval.py:242-251).

verified.title: every heartbeat beat is emitted before any record is read, so a score run that dies mid-read is judged `done` and never gets a failed row

verified.title: A failure in one task's env.close() escapes the per-task guard and ends the whole piece
verified.detail: The per-task guard (`except Exception` at agent/loop.py:163) covers the body only; `env.close()` runs in the `finally` at agent/loop.py:175-176, outside it. An exception out of `Environment.close` therefore propagates through the `for split, task_id, seed in triples` loop and out of `main`, so the piece stops and every remaining triple of its rotation is never walked. This is exactly the failure the clause exists to prevent (ticket 11 step 3: "Any other exception from one task is caught, recorded and walked past"; errata line 66; the file's own comment on line 163). The record of the task that failed is complete (its `final` row was already written); what is lost is the rest of that piece's walk.

verified.title: jobs/launch.py's own liveness test is not fail-closed: it ignores the failed-host set registry.live_sessions() returns
verified.detail: `_piece_alive` is `bool(session) and session in live_sessions`. `registry.live_sessions()` returns a `_ProbedSessions` carrying `failed_hosts`, and `registry._alive_on` (jobs/registry.py:515-521) implements 3.4's rule - "a failed or timed-out ssh counts as ... alive for a session, so an unclear probe never ... declares a piece dead" - by reporting a piece on a failed host alive. `jobs/launch.py` never reads `failed_hosts` (no occurrence in the file), so both of its users lose the rule.
